title: Joseph T.M. @ Sony vs Nirmala Raphel @ Mary Nirmala on 3 November, 2010

paragraphs.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF KERALA AT ERNAKULAM

 PRESENT:

 THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE ANTONY DOMINIC
 &
 THE HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE P.D.RAJAN

 TUESDAY, THE 3RD DAY OF SEPTEMBER 2013/12TH BHADRA, 1935

 Mat.Appeal.No. 264 of 2011 ( )
 -------------------------------
AGAINST THE ORDER/JUDGMENT IN OPDIV 1137/2005 of FAMILY COURT, ALAPPUZHA
 DATED 03-11-2010
APPELLANT(S)/RESPONDENT:
-------------------------------------------
 JOSEPH T.M. @ SONY
 AGED 38 YEARS,
 THANNIPPILLY,SEBASTIAN ROAD,
 KALOOR P.O., KOCHI.

 BY ADV. SMT.K.V.RASHMI

RESPONDENT(S)/PETITIONER:
--------------------------------------------

 NIRMALA RAPHEL @ MARY NIRMALA,
 AGED 31 YEARS, THYKOOTTATHIL HOUSE,
 AROOR P.O., ALAPPUZHA,
 PIN 688 534.

 BY ADV. SRI.BABU S. NAIR
 BY ADV. SMT.SMITHA BABU

 THIS MATRIMONIAL APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 03-09-2013,
 THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:


acd



 ANTONY DOMINIC & P.D. RAJAN, JJ.
 -------------------------------------------
 Mat. Appeal No.264 of 2011
 ----------------------------------------------
 Dated this the 3rd day of September, 2013

 JUDGMENT

Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned

counsel appearing for the respondent.

2. This appeal arises from the judgment and decree passed

by the Family Court, Alappuzha in O.P.No.1137/2005.

3. The appellant and the respondent are husband and wife.

Their marriage was solemnized on 29.9.2003. In the wedlock, a

female child was born on 26.4.2004. On 13.7.2005, the respondent

wife filed the O.P. seeking divorce urging grounds of cruelty and that

the appellant was incurably of unsound mind as provided under

 Section 10(1)(iii) of the Indian Divorce Act, 1869.

4. Before the Family Court, evidence was adduced by both

sides by examining Pws 1 to 3 and Rws1 and 2. Exts.A1 to A14, B1 to

B3 and Exts.X1 and X2 were also marked. The Family Court by

judgment dated 3rd November 2010, disposed of the O.P. rejecting the

case of the appellant under Section 10(1)(iii) of the Indian Divorce Act

and accepting the case on the ground of cruelty, dissolving the

Mat.Appeal No.264/11 2

marriage by a decree of divorce. It is aggrieved by this judgment,

the appellant husband has filed this appeal.

5. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that the

evidence adduced in the case did not make out a case of cruelty and

according to her, the incident that happened on 8.1.2005 and relied

on by the Family Court was a stage managed one and therefore,

could not have been relied on by the respondent.

6. Insofar as her first contention that the respondent did

not make out a case of cruelty is concerned, we were referred to

the evidence of respondent, who was examined as PW1. In her

proof affidavit, which was filed in lieu of the chief examination, she

has narrated various instances of cruelty. The evidence also shows

that, though she was cross examined in detail, nothing was brought

out to disbelieve her testimony. It was in such circumstances, the

Family Court has accepted the case of cruelty.

7. Admittedly, the appellant is a patient of Psychosis with

paranoid features. It is in evidence that he has been undergoing

treatment from 1998 and the evidence of RW2, the doctor, shows

that he is still undergoing treatment. There is evidence, which

indicates that the appellant treated the respondent with suspicion.

There is also evidence, which indicated various acts of physical

cruelty. One of the instances happened on 8.1.2005, when he is

alleged to have attempted to kill the respondent by himself with a

Mat.Appeal No.264/11 3

knife. The fact that incident had happened, has been deposed not

only by PW1 wife but also by her father, who was examined as

RW3. It is in evidence that he was thereafter taken to Sacred

Hospital, Painkulam where he was treated as an inpatient till

11.2.2005. This fact that he has undergone treatment has been

deposed by RW2, Chief Psychiatrist of the Hospital.

8. As far the case of the appellant that the incident on

happened on 8.1.2005 and his hospitalisation were stage managed

one is concerned, from the evidence what we noticed is that

immediately after the incident on 8.1.2005, the parents of the

respondent took her home. Thereafter, the matter was

communicated to the police and it was none other than the in-laws

of the appellant himself, who took him to the Sacred Hospital and

got him admitted. He was removed from his house in the presence

of his parents. His parents did not complain about his removal. On

the other hand, they also allowed him to continue in the hospital till

11.2.2005. If as stated by the appellant, the incident and

treatment were stage managed one, things would not have moved

as smoothly or peacefully as is evident from the records.

9. Therefore, in the light of these facts, we are unable to

accept the case of the appellant that the incident happened on

8.1.2005 was a stage managed one.

10. Evidently, therefore, this is the case where the

Mat.Appeal No.264/11 4

respondent was treated with cruelty and that allegation of the

respondent was proved before the Family Court, not only with the

evidence of Pws1 to 3 but also with the expert medical evidence

that is available. In such a situation, the Family Court justified in

granting a decree of divorce.

11. We do not find any illegality in the order passed by the

Family Court justifying interference of this Court.
The Mat. Appeal will stand dismissed.

ANTONY DOMINIC, JUDGE




 P.D. RAJAN, JUDGE.
